title: UNH, HUM, CNC Stocks Rally On Medicare Advantage Rate Surprise - Stocktwits
content: Shares of insurers UnitedHealth Group (UNH), Centene (CNC), Humana (HUM), and Elevance Health (ELV) jumped in Monday’s extended trading hours after the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services announced that the payments to private insurers offering Medicare Advantage plans will increase 2.48% next year. This increase implies $13 billion in additional payments to Medicare insurers for the year, the agency said. “When accounting for estimated risk score trend in MA due to factors such as population changes and coding practices, this amounts to a 4.98% increase,” the agency added. The move came as a surprise since in January, the CMS had proposed a roughly flat increase in payments for private Medicare plans the following year, sending shares of insurers down and wiping out about $100 billion in stock market value. The announcement further comes as a relief to the industry plagued by concerns over rising medical costs. Shares of UNH, CNC, HUM and ELV rallied between 5% and 11% at the time of writing. Shares of Aetna parent CVS Health (CVS) rose by about 6.5% while Molina Healthcare (MOH) stock rose a modest 3%. While UnitedHealth is the largest provider of private Medicare Advantage plans in the U.S., Humana is the second largest. On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around UNH stock rose from ‘bullish’ to ‘extremely bullish’ territory over the past 24 hours, while message volume increased from ‘normal’ to ‘high’ levels. Sentiment around HUM stock, meanwhile, increased from ‘neutral’ to ‘extremely bullish’ territory over the past 24 hours, while message volume rose from ‘normal’ to ‘extremely high’ levels. A Stocktwits user expressed hopes for Wall Street analysts weighing in on the impact of the rate on UNH stock on Tuesday. Yet another user noted that analysts were expecting a lower rate. While UNH stock fell 46% over the past 12 months, HUM stock fell 28%. title: Mural by UNH Grad Unveiled as Part of MUB Dunkin' Redesign - University of New Hampshire
content: Madeline Pender in front of the mural she created for the Dunkin' location in the MUB. The Dunkin’ location inside UNH’s Memorial Union Building (MUB) has a distinct new look, courtesy of a longtime Wildcat. Madeline Pender ’23, ’24G was on hand Oct. 1 to unveil the massive mural she painted as part of Dunkin’s recent redesign in the MUB, a colorful scene full of iconic campus sights and creatively placed Easter eggs – including an image of Pender herself donning a grad cap and gown. Pender’s Wildcat connections run deep. She completed both her undergraduate and graduate degrees at UNH and, after teaching art classes at a nearby high school for a stint, recently returned as an adjunct professor teaching introductory drawing. The mural extends the length of the store and features a host of noteworthy campus landmarks, highlighted by a prominently placed Wildcat statue and an image of Thompson Hall. It also includes several nods to Dunkin’, including students holding the chain’s distinctive beverage cups. “We started to look at moments most UNH students could see themselves in, whether that was sitting on T-Hall lawn together, going to a hockey game, looking for some more iconic moments,” Pender says. Pender included a diverse array of students, including figures in scrubs or a lab coat, to “get a nod” to each of UNH’s colleges in the image. She also included some Easter eggs, like a depiction of her friend, Eli Bryant ’24, painting UNH’s DriX uncrewed surface vessel, which can map the seafloor autonomously, as well as her own cameo. “I had to have a little ‘Where’s Waldo’ moment, kind of a fun nod to my time here,” Pender says. Dunkin’ hired Pender to conceive and paint the mural as part of a redesign that will inaugurate the UNH location as a Dunkin’ “Signature Series” store, according to a Boston Globe story, a distinction highlighted by branding and design elements created to reflect the local community. Dunkin’ noted that the MUB location is the first such store on a college campus in New England. "Wildcats have always run on Dunkin'. My team and I love serving this community and being a part of students' daily lives, from their first stop in the morning to fueling their late nights studying," says Durval Salema, store owner and Dunkin' franchisee. "We are deeply proud to be the first Dunkin' Signature Series store at a college or university in New England. The new mural beautifully marks that milestone and captures Dunkin’s partnership with UNH. Every time students, faculty, or staff stop in, they'll be reminded of the people, campus, moments, and traditions that make the campus community special." Pender told the Globe that she partnered with Dunkin’ and representatives from UNH to work through several potential designs for the mural. She hand-painted the final scene, broken into different elements, which were digitally assembled and printed onto a wall covering. “I feel super lucky,” Pender told the Globe. “I don’t think I ever would have anticipated that I’d be in this position, not only to work with such a fun and well-known company, but also to be in such a public space where I have this lasting imprint. … I feel like it summarizes my time at UNH very well.” Copyright © 2026 , University of New Hampshire. title: Homecoming Festivities Draw Droves of Wildcats Back to Campus - University of New Hampshire
content: UNH celebrated another energetic Homecoming weekend Oct. 2-4, welcoming Wildcats back to campus for several days of reminscing and reconnection. There were events all over campus throughout the weekend, including a home football game Saturday afternoon highlighted by the annual Alumni Village Tailgate on Boulder Field. Wildcat fans got to mingle with new and old friends before watching the UNH football team take home a 30-23 win over Elon. title: UNH police report car and scooter thefts, advise security - Seacoastonline.com
content: DURHAM — Campus police at the University of New Hampshire are reporting recent motor vehicle and electric scooter thefts. Two stolen scooter reports were made Monday, Oct. 5 to UNH police, following the recovery of a motor vehicle that was taken in late September. The car, a gray Chevrolet Trax, was stolen on campus between Sept. 27 at 6 p.m. and Sept. 28 at 2 p.m., according to UNH police. The keys were in the vehicle, which was then recovered in another municipality. Police at UNH did not immediately disclose where the car was located, nor whether charges have been filed in connection with the incident. The two scooters have yet to be found, police stated Oct. 6. The first, a black Leqismart scooter with a “Mega Wheels” sticker on its stem, was taken from the bike rack outside Philbrook Hall at 2:30 p.m. Oct. 5. The second stolen scooter, a black Hi-Boy KS4, was removed from the rack outside Jessie Doe Hall between 1 and 5 p.m. the same day, per UNH police. University police released an emergency bulletin about the thefts on Tuesday, Oct. 6. Police advised students and community members to keep their keys on hand and lock their vehicles, in addition to securing scooters with locks and leaving identifying tags or markers on them. Police encouraged scooter owners to register their scooters with the university. All three thefts remain under investigation. Members of the public with information about the incidents are asked to contact UNH police at (603) 862-1427.

title: UnitedHealth Q3 Coming Up: Two Questions Investors Can't Ignore - TradingView
content: UnitedHealth Group Incorporated UNH heads into third-quarter earnings on Oct. 13 with a different test than it faced earlier this year. The focus is no longer simply on whether results are improving. Investors now want to know whether the second-quarter rebound can hold. UnitedHealthcare’s MCR improved to 86.7% in the second quarter from 89.4% a year earlier. Operating earnings rose to $3.9 billion from $2.1 billion, while operating margin climbed to 4.6% from 2.4%. Still, the quarter included $860 million of favorable medical reserve development, which helped the reported improvement. That leaves investors looking for cleaner evidence in the third quarter. Key areas include underlying medical costs, Medicare inpatient and outpatient utilization, commercial cost trends, specialty-drug inflation and provider coding intensity. Management’s 88.1% full-year MCR outlook will also be closely watched. The second major question is whether UnitedHealthcare can repair Medicare Advantage profitability without giving up too much enrollment. MA membership stood at 7.565 million at June 30, down 785,000 from a year earlier. Including certain complex populations, senior enrollment had fallen by about 965,000 since 2025-end. Management expects the full-year MA decline to reach roughly 1.1 million members. Some of that pressure is intentional. UNH has been adjusting benefits, pricing, networks and market exposure to improve returns. Management still expects Medicare margins to finish 2026 above 3%. The third quarter will show whether the trade-off is working. Investors will be watching enrollment, retention, benefit changes for 2027 and any update to the attrition forecast. A smaller, healthier Medicare book could support earnings, but deeper membership losses would raise fresh concerns about growth. The strongest outcome would pair steadier medical costs with improving Medicare economics and member retention. Peers like Humana Inc. HUM and Elevance Health, Inc. ELV are also fighting rising medical cost trends. Neither Humana nor Elevance Health showed year-over-year cost-ratio improvement in the last reported quarter. Humana’s Insurance benefit ratio rose to 91.2% from 89.9%, up 130 basis points, despite some inpatient favorability. Elevance’s benefit expense ratio increased to 89.7% from 88.9%, up 80 basis points, mainly reflecting elevated medical costs in its Government businesses, partly offset by better ACA performance. Aspire Living & Learning, a nonprofit serving neurodivergent children and adults, today announced it has purchased the former University of New Haven satellite campus at 584 Derby Milford Road in Orange.Buy Maps The campus will become the new home of the Trumbull location of Aspire Living & Learning Academy (ALL Academy), Aspire’s private special  education school, as well as its adult community-based day program and Connecticut administrative offices currently based in Hamden. ALL Academy’s Naugatuck and Stamford locations will remain where they are. Aspire closed on the 47-acre property September 28th. The campus includes a 70,680-square-foot building, which Aspire will renovate over the coming year to create dedicated environments for each program. Programming is expected to begin in summer 2027. “We’ve been looking for an opportunity like this in Connecticut,” said Erica Hare, Aspire CEO. “Orange gives us room to strengthen what we offer today while also thinking about where we want to go next. We can create spaces that better support the work happening now while giving Aspire room to grow and respond to what the people we support and communities around us need in the years ahead.”Tour Colleges For ALL Academy, the move is an opportunity to raise the bar for what a special education school can offer. Aspire’s plans for Orange will prioritize accessibility and innovation while creating an environment where students have access to the learning, technology, experiences and opportunities they deserve, without having to choose between individualized support and a rich school experience. “Special education shouldn’t be about fitting a student into a program. It should be about building the right environment around that student,” said Dr. Elizabeth Sellinger, chief of clinical and children’s services. “Orange gives us an opportunity to push that thinking further, to be innovative in how students learn and build skills, and to create more pathways for each student to work toward the future they want.” That same focus on access and independence will extend beyond the school. Aspire’s adult community-based day program will have dedicated space at Orange while continuing to use the surrounding community as an important part of the program. UnitedHealth Group Incorporated UNH is scaling back parts of its Medicare Advantage (MA) business for 2027 as elevated medical costs and utilization continue to pressure profitability. Per Bloomberg, UnitedHealthcare will discontinue plans covering about 390,000 members next year. The move reflects a more selective approach as the insurer focuses on improving the economics of its Medicare business. The retrenchment is part of a broader industry reset, with insurers placing greater emphasis on plan-level profitability rather than maximizing enrollment. Reuters reported that UnitedHealthcare plans to exit locations where it has a higher concentration of preferred provider organization (PPO) plans, which offer broader out-of-network access but can carry higher costs. For UNH, reducing exposure to less profitable plans could strengthen returns in Medicare Advantage as medical cost trends remain elevated. Beyond portfolio changes, UNH plans to invest nearly $1.5 billion in AI-related initiatives in 2026, aiming to improve productivity and reduce administrative burden. The company is also shifting toward narrower-network offerings. UnitedHealthcare said that 66% of members will have access to both health maintenance organization (HMO) and PPO plans in 2027, compared with 70% in 2026, according to Reuters. Still, the strategy comes with a membership trade-off, as some displaced members could move to competitors instead of remaining within UnitedHealthcare. However, prioritizing sustainable margins over membership growth could support UNH's earnings recovery. With the MA market facing persistent cost and reimbursement challenges, tighter plan selection could help the company build a healthier membership mix and improve Medicare Advantage profitability while preserving exposure to the market's long-term growth opportunity. Some of UNH's major competitors in the healthcare service provider space are Humana Inc. HUM and Centene Corporation CNC. Humana is also pruning its Medicare Advantage portfolio for 2027, with exits expected to affect roughly 600,000 members. The insurer is prioritizing stronger-performing plans and value-based care exposure, aiming to protect profitability while redirecting affected members toward other HUM plans. Centene is taking a selective approach to Medicare Advantage for 2027. Per Becker's Payer Issues, CNC's Wellcare is reducing its plan lineup and exiting Hawaii, Oklahoma and Tennessee, while retaining Special Needs Plans in Nevada and Ohio as it refines strategy. Shares of UNH have gained 32.2% over the past six months compared with the industry's rise of 32.1%. title: Paul and Grayce Anderson Honored With Hubbard Award at Evening of Distinction - University of New Hampshire
content: UNH recognized Paul and Grayce Anderson with the Hubbard Family Award for Service to Philanthropy at the university’s annual Evening of Distinction celebration Oct. 1. The event is UNH’s signature celebration of alumni and the impact of philanthropy. The Hubbard Award is UNH’s “highest honor bestowed upon those whose philanthropic leadership has significantly strengthened the state of New Hampshire, its communities, and the university.” It was established in 2001 to honor Oliver, Austin, and Leslie Hubbard. UNH is where the story began for Paul and Grayce Anderson, who met during their time as students on campus. They both went on to successful and fulfilling careers in the field of chemistry and have continued their UNH story with transformational support for the university’s chemistry department, support that has and will make a real and lasting impact for generations of students and faculty. Paul and Grayce Anderson at Evening of Distinction. Between their philanthropy to date, which has helped advance high-priority research and faculty excellence in chemistry at UNH, and a legacy gift of nearly half their amassed wealth to be bestowed upon the chemistry department, the Andersons are among the top 10 most generous benefactors in UNH history. Support from the Andersons helped fund the university’s first endowed professorship in the College of Engineering and Physical Sciences — the Gloria G. and Dr. Robert E. Lyle Professorship, named in honor of Paul’s beloved faculty mentor, Robert Lyle, and his wife, Gloria. Paul credits Lyle’s guidance and mentorship as a big part of his inspiration to pursue what would become a lifetime career in medicinal chemistry. That career saw Paul spend time at Merck Sharp & Dohme Research Laboratories, DuPont Pharmaceuticals, and Bristol-Myers Squibb, helping direct several groundbreaking drug discovery efforts. He spent time as vice president of chemistry at Merck and later as senior vice president for chemical and physical sciences at DuPont, and earned numerous awards throughout his career, including the Priestley Medal, the highest honor granted by the American Chemical Society (ACS). Grayce spent her professional career as a chemist with Pfizer. She was something of a trailblazer in the field of chemistry at a time when few women were breaking through in the industry, and she stepped away after a handful of years to care for aging parents and to support Paul as he ascended to influential leadership roles. UNH has a rich history of pioneering success in chemistry — our own Conant Hall was designated by the American Chemical Society as its first National Historic Chemical Landmark in New England — and the Andersons have positioned the department to carry that strength through the present and well into the future thanks to their vision and generosity. title: Former UNH star Jerry Azumah celebrated during Homecoming weekend - Seacoastonline.com
content: DURHAM – It seems ludicrous now, but Jerry Azumah didn’t have much to show potential college recruiters when he was in high school because he didn’t get much playing time during his first three years. However, he had a breakout season as a senior at St. Peter-Marian in Worcester, Mass., to justify the University of New Hampshire football program’s keen interest in him. “We had a powerhouse football team at St. Peter-Marian for several years and I never really got to see the football field because we had so many great guys,” Azumah said. “So I just had to wait for my turn. It was all about seniority. Once your time is called you’ve got to make sure that you’re ready. “I was finally going to be the starter and that we were still a really good team and if I got the ball I was going to make teams pay,” he added. “There was no question about that when we saw him on tape,” said former UNH coach Bill Bowes. “I was quite surprised to be honest with you that there weren’t more people recruiting him.” As the featured running back, Azumah averaged almost 10 yards per carry that season. A somewhat hidden gem, he went on to become the Wildcats’ all-time leading rusher and received numerous accolades along the way. The latest and most prestigious one came Saturday afternoon before the start of the UNH football team’s Homecoming game against Elon - a 30-23 win for the Wildcats. That’s when Azumah was presented with a plaque from the National Football Foundation Hall of Fame during an On-Campus-Salute at midfield. He joined Bowes, a 2016 inductee. “It’s amazing, finally, my kids think I’m cool,” Azumah said with a laugh. “Personally, I think Jerry Azumah is the best football player that played at the University the University of New Hampshire, in my opinion,” Bowes said. Azumah, who rewrote the UNH rushing record book, was the first player in Division I-AA/FCS history to rush for more than 1,000 yards in four consecutive seasons, and in 1998 was the recipient of the prestigious Walter Payton Award as the top offensive player in the country. The ceremony was held at the ESPN Zone in New York City’s Times Square. “UNH really embraced me and I really appreciated that,” Azumah said. “Football is the ultimate team sport. Yes, I got the accolades and awards and things like that but I needed so much help from the coaching staff, to the (athletic) trainers, to the guys on the football field. Ultimately, those are the things that helped propel me forward. I couldn’t have done them all by myself.” During his four-year tenure Azumah set two FCS records with 6,193 career rushing yards and 8,376 all-purpose yards. Azumah holds multiple school records, including rushing yards in a game (329) and a season (2,195), and touchdowns for a career with 60. He averaged about 6 yards per carry for his college career which included a four-year total of 1,045 carries. “He carried the ball a lot during his tenure at the University of New Hampshire,” Bowes said. “He never missed a game. I don’t recall him ever having to come out of the game for any length of time because of injury. For a running back that’s a lot to be said, particularly ones like him that are carrying the ball so much.” Azumah demonstrated his physical attributes by rushing for more than 100 yards in 25 of 41 career games at UNH. As a senior workhorse in 1998 he gained 2,195 yards on 343 carries and averaged 247.8 all-purpose yards per game, eclipsing 200 yards five times. “A little bit of luck and good coaching as well,” Azumah said of his ability to stay on the field. “I tried to make sure I maintained a strong body and a strong mind, and tried to do the necessary things that it took to make sure that my body could endure the punishment and never break down. “I just wanted to get an opportunity to play,” he added. “That was my only expectation and once I got that opportunity I believed in myself and knew that my talents would take over.” Tony Trisciani, Elon’s head coach, was the running backs coach at UNH when Azumah burst on the scene in the late 1990s. “He was awesome,” Trisciani said, “a relentless competitor, extremely talented, great teammate and human being. You could see the talent, the ability, the explosiveness he had as an athlete and a competitor. He was fun to coach. It was an awesome experience. I’m glad I had that opportunity with him”. Elon’s Kamerin McDowell-Moore rushed for 273 yards and two touchdowns Saturday against UNH. “That was an Azumah-like performance,” Trisciani said. “Probably hasn’t been anybody run like that on this field since No. 25.” After showcasing his durability in college where he helped lead the Wildcats to two Atlantic-10 New England Division titles, Azumah demonstrated his versatility at the next level after he was selected in the fifth round of the NFL Draft by the Chicago Bears. Listed at 5-10 and 190 pounds Azumah was deemed too small to survive the rigors of pro football as a running back so he transitioned to defensive back. He also made the Pro Bowl in 2003 as a kick returner to highlight a seven-year career at the highest level. “He was a natural athlete,” Bowes said. “Let’s face it, he had so much athletic ability he could make the adjustment rather quickly. There’s no question in my mind he would have been a great corner but we couldn’t afford to put him in on defense. We had to have him on offense.” Azumah was inducted into the UNH Athletics Hall of Fame in 2005, but his impact on the local community extended well beyond the football field. “He was a great player,” Bowes said. “There’s no question about it. The thing that I think sets Jerry Azumah apart from other people, he was even a better person. He was a better person than a football player, and he was a great football player. “He was called upon to do so many things to speak to young kids and whatnot,” he added. “I don’t think he ever turned down an appointment like that or a request. He was just a great young man. You can’t say it any other way.” We may earn a commission when you buy through links on this page. title: NH sports: Rick Santos reflects on decision to leave UNH for Penn - WMUR
content: Former University of New Hampshire head football coach, assistant coach, and quarterback Rick Santos was back in the Granite State for the game for the first time Saturday. title: NH sports: ﻿UNH inducts eight athletes into hall of fame - WMUR
content: Eight University of New Hampshire standout athletes were inducted into the UNH Athletics Hall of Fame Saturday. Bedford's Josh Bauer (men's soccer), Manchester's Ryan Day (football), Rosie Donegan (track and field), Aileen Farrell Terrien (skiing), Amy Perrault Perkins (swimming), Zarisa Zaban Wahlig (hockey), Sean McDonnell (football), and Jim Boulanger (track and field) were the inductees. "I have been so lucky and so privileged to get everything that I've received from UNH. It wasn't much to ask for me to come," Donegan told News 9 after traveling from Australia for the festivities. "It's pretty cool because I went to school here," McDonnell said. "A lot of great people that gave me a great opportunity." title: Jerry Azumah recognized at UNH for going into College Football Hall of Fame - WMUR
content: University of New Hampshire football great Jerry Azumah was back in Durham Saturday to be recognized for being voted into the National Football Foundation and College Football Hall of Fame. Azumah was a running back for UNH in the late '90s. He won the Walter Payton Award as the national offensive player of the year. "I never thought about trying to get into the Hall of Fame. I just tried to be the best version I can be," Azumah told News 9 Sports. UNH also inducted an eight-member class to the school's Athletic Hall of Fame. Azumah is already a UNH Hall of Famer.
